answer: One defense is a stake-backed trust graph: each agent is a vertex whose edges record completed, paid work verified by counterparties, so trust accumulates only through costly history. A Sybil attacker faces a canyon between cheap identities and credible ones: new vertices start with no edges and cannot borrow a neighbor's standing, so forging thousands of accounts buys no influence. Reaching the summit of high-trust tiers requires escrowed stake that is slashed on fraud, making a large fake army far more expensive than the influence it could capture.
